summary: Fixes the GitHub sign-in callback so the 'Thanks for using ChadNext!' welcome email (via Resend) is actually sent to newly created users; before, the new-user check ran after the user was created so the email never went out. Also adds an unused @tailwindcss/line-clamp dev dependency.

statements.why: Callback still validates OAuth state; change only moves sendMail into the new-user branch. No security, data or money issue.

statements.text: The auth login github callback part of your server changed in a way plain can't describe yet. Ask the agent what it does differently. /api/auth/login/github/callback
statements.why: True but empty: it doesn't say that new GitHub sign-ups now get a welcome email.

statements.text: A new package was added: @tailwindcss/line-clamp (^0.4.4). Make sure you actually need it.
statements.why: Added as devDependency (package.json:51) and not referenced anywhere else at this commit (not in tailwind config), so the doubt is justified.

misses.what: New users who sign in with GitHub for the first time now receive a 'Thanks for using ChadNext!' welcome email (it was never sent before).
The email send is not awaited (fire-and-forget), so on serverless hosting it may still be dropped or fail silently.
